title: Theo and the Orchard
premise: In the winter of 1794, as the Republic devours its own, Elodie Crane carries sealed dispatches through occupied countryside, hiding in plain sight as a hired hand at a failing orchard. When Theo Marchand arrives bearing a letter in the handwriting of General Aubertin — officially executed months before — he becomes entangled in a plot to smuggle the general's surviving evidence out of France. To honor a peacetime promise to the man now branded an enemy, Theo must choose between loyalty to his own family's safety and the truth that could save or hang them all; the book ends at the century's turn with the dispatches delivered, Elodie and Theo choosing each other over duty, and the orchard burning behind them as they cross into exile.
about_author: Marguerite Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing émigré letters in provincial French collections. She writes historical fiction from a farmhouse she restored herself, where she keeps an orchard of heirloom pears.

chapters.title: The Pruning Knife
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Winter work at the Vasseur orchard conceals her courier identity; she memorizes routes by the rhythm of pruning. A patrol passes, and she hides dispatches inside a grafting kit. Emotional beat: quiet vigilance, the cost of being invisible.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Road
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Fleeing Paris after his brother's arrest, Theo arrives at the orchard seeking work and shelter. He recognizes nothing yet, but the farmhands watch him too closely. Emotional beat: exhaustion meeting wary hospitality.

chapters.title: The Handwriting of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Sorting crates, Theo finds a letter in the unmistakable hand of General Aubertin — the man who once saved his family and was guillotined in autumn. The letter names Elodie. Emotional beat: disbelief sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Hides
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She discovers Theo has seen the letter and must decide whether to kill his credibility, recruit him, or run. Instead she tests him with a false errand. Emotional beat: calculation warring with a flicker of trust.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, flashback woven in. Years earlier, Aubertin asked Theo to promise: if ever a letter came in his hand, deliver it whole, to no one else. Theo recalls the garden, the handshake, the war not yet begun. Emotional beat: the weight of old vows.

chapters.title: The Committee's Shadow
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A local agent, Delacour, arrives auditing farms for 'unregistered persons.' Elodie forges papers while Theo plays the dull laborer. Emotional beat: performance under pressure, terror disguised as boredom.

chapters.title: Graft and Rootstock
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Working beside Theo, she teaches him grafting as cover for teaching him courier signals. Their guarded intimacy begins. Emotional beat: two lonely people finding a shared language.

chapters.title: The Letter's Second Half
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The letter references documents proving the Republic's generals were betrayed from within — and a rendezvous at the coast before the year ends. But half the page is missing. Emotional beat: hope complicated by incompleteness.

chapters.title: Delacour Returns
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Delacour lingers, suspicious of Theo's Paris accent, and requisitions the orchard's stores. Elodie must feed the enemy to deflect him. Emotional beat: humiliation endured strategically.

chapters.title: Brother's Keeper
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. News reaches him: his brother will be released if Theo informs on the orchard's 'traffic.' He burns the summons and says nothing to Elodie. Emotional beat: guilt taking root like blight.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The first hard frost forces the harvest in; the whole household works through the night. In the cellar afterward, Elodie tells Theo part of her truth. Emotional beat: warmth stolen from a cold season.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo realizes Delacour holds the torn half of Aubertin's letter, taken from his brother's cell. Retrieving it means walking into the agent's hands. Emotional beat: resolve crystallizing around fear.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Cider
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie confronts Theo about his silence; furious, frightened, they argue, then plan together. She proposes using Delacour's greed against him. Emotional beat: conflict transmuted into partnership.

chapters.title: The Trap at the Mill
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The exchange goes wrong — Delacour expected them, but so did Aubertin's surviving adjutant, who kills the agent and vanishes with the page. Emotional beat: chaos, relief curdling into new danger.

chapters.title: Enemy of the Republic
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. With Delacour dead, the network is compromised; Aubertin is revealed alive, hidden, and now doubly damned. Theo learns the full scope of the promise he made. Emotional beat: awe and vertigo.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie's handler orders her to abandon the general and burn the evidence — the mission is dead, survival is paramount. She refuses quietly. Emotional beat: duty breaking against conscience.

chapters.title: The Long Road North
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The three flee through snow toward the coast, pursued by both sides. Aubertin, ill and unrepentant, tests Theo's promise daily. Emotional beat: endurance, and love admitted in whispers.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Harbor Town
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The adjutant sells them out to save himself; Aubertin is taken. Theo faces the choice: the documents or the man. Emotional beat: the promise made in peacetime meets its price.

chapters.title: Fire in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. Theo trades the evidence's location to free Aubertin while Elodie runs the real dispatches aboard a neutral ship. Soldiers torch the orchard as cover. Emotional beat: everything burned to save what matters.

chapters.title: Before the Century Turns
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. On the deck at midnight, New Year's guns fire across the water. The dispatches are delivered; the betrayal will surface in foreign papers by spring. Emotional beat: exhausted triumph, grief for what stayed behind.

chapters.title: Exile
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Aubertin, freed and broken, chooses a quiet death abroad rather than return. Theo and Elodie bury him under a pear tree he planted long ago in England. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into rootedness.

chapters.title: Spring Grafting
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Elodie's POV. A year later, the two tend a small new orchard, grafting cuttings smuggled from the old one. A letter arrives bearing familiar handwriting — the future is still dangerous, but they face it together. Emotional beat: hope, hard-won and seasonal.
